messages:
inc-bot: Paging #incidents — P1: Partial egress failures observed from us-east-1b (multiple customers). Alert: elevated 5xx to external APIs and outbound connection failures. Link: https://dash.internal/alerts/12345

emma.h: Acked. Seeing spike in 504s from our outbound proxies about 04:12 UTC. Traces show timeouts on external API calls originating from AZ-b subnets.

rajesh.n: I noticed a terraform apply merged ~04:10 that changed route table associations for subnets in us-east-1b. Possible bad rollout.

mike_g: Confirm — I ran a tiny standardization apply this morning to re-associate subnets to the consolidated route table. Rolling back now.

linh: Graphs: AZ-B egress packet drops + conntrack errors on NAT instances/gw. NACL snapshot shows ephemeral ports blocked on one of the ACL rules. Investigating if both the route change and an ACL drift coincided.

tanya_cs: Customer impact: at least 7 customers reporting increased errors in external integrations. Some feature degradations (webhooks/external syncs). Working on a status page draft.

deploy-bot: Triggered rollback job: terraform apply -target=aws_route_table_association.rollback (job id: 78910). Operation: replacing association rtbassoc-0a1b2c3d -> expect propagation in ~30s.

inc-bot: Escalation: P1 -> paging infra/networking/sre. Please acknowledge.

mike_g: Running command to re-associate now:
```
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-0a1b2c3d --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234
```
Should be quick.

linh: Confirmed route table on subnet-azb-prod-2 was switched to rtb-missing-egress which lacks 0.0.0.0/0->NAT/GW. That explains the outbound blackhole. NACL rule that dropped ephemeral ports likely a separate drift.

rajesh.n: If the NAT route was removed, we should recreate it if assoc rollback doesn't immediately fix sessions. Command to recreate route:
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0d4e5f
```
I'll be ready to run that.

emma.h: Oncall handoff in ~25m, I'll stay until rollback confirmed. Rajesh please take lead after.

mike_g: replace-route-table-association returned success (rtbassoc-0a1b2c3d). Propagation visible.

linh: Metrics: error-rate in AZ-B down from 18% -> 3% over the last 2 minutes. Latency for outbound calls also returning to baseline.

tanya_cs: Status page update draft prepared. Will post 'Investigation -> Mitigated' once metrics stable. Notifying impacted customers via the incident template.

rajesh.n: I re-added missing NAT route as a precaution:
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0d4e5f
```
Route created.

mike_g: Pushed revert PR to the infra repo to avoid further drift: https://git.internal/repo/pull/456 (includes note to add a guardrail).

linh: Doing sanity checks: curl to external endpoints from instances in AZ-B now succeed. Sampled logs show 200s for previously failing requests. Monitoring for 15m.

inc-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity reduced to P2. Please prepare postmortem and action items.

emma.h: Handing off pager to Rajesh for rotation. Rajesh, please own the follow-up and postmortem. I'll remain on-call until the scheduled handoff.

rajesh.n: Taking handoff. Immediate root-cause summary: accidental route table association to a RTB missing default egress route during a terraform standardization change + an unrelated NACL drift. Action plan: 1) blameless postmortem, 2) add CI tests to validate route table includes default egress to NAT/GW, 3) add Terraform guardrail to prevent unintended assoc flips, 4) add NACL audit in infra scanning.

tanya_cs: Status page updated to 'Mitigated' at 04:35 UTC. Customers acknowledged — no urgent escalations after mitigation.

linh: Follow-ups for runbook: include quick check commands and the two-step rollback pattern (replace-route-table-association then create-route if needed). I'll add examples.

mike_g: I'll own the Terraform fix and the revert PR. Adding a canary apply to staging before prod in the pipeline.

emma.h: Thanks all for the quick response. Please link the postmortem here when ready. :thumbsup:
